slot.brief: Given compound statements built with ∧, ∨, negations, identify which option is logically equivalent to the given statement; simplify with De Morgan's laws.

stem:
Which statement is logically equivalent to $
eg[p\wedge(q\vee r)]$?
options:
$
eg p\vee(
eg q\wedge
eg r)$

$
eg p\wedge(
eg q\vee
eg r)$

$
eg p\vee(
eg q\vee
eg r)$

verdicts.working: By De Morgan’s laws, ¬[p ∧ (q ∨ r)] = ¬p ∨ (¬q ∧ ¬r), which is option A.

working:
$
eg[p\wedge(q\vee r)]\equiv
eg p\vee
eg(q\vee r)\equiv
eg p\vee(
eg q\wedge
eg r)$.

Independent check: By De Morgan’s laws, ¬[p ∧ (q ∨ r)] = ¬p ∨ (¬q ∧ ¬r), which is option A.
